newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Violence erupts at Australian race row party launch.
newsitem.headline: Violence erupts at Australian race row party launch.

text.p: Australian police on Tuesday blamed a small group of activists for violence at a launch meeting for race row politician Pauline Hanson's One Nation party at which several people were injured.
Up to 1,500 protesters disrupted the meeting on Monday night at Dandenong, just outside Melbourne, attended by 150 pro-Hanson supporters but not Hanson herself.
Police said a small group of protesters, some wearing black balaclavas, were behind the violence. Protesters threw potatoes, eggs and urine-filled ballons.
"There was a small core of protesters that got out of hand," said a police spokesman. "I think there was a bit of overreaction there by those who oppose the One Nation party."

One pro-Hanson supporter, a 60-year-old man, was taken unconscious to hospital after suffering cuts to the head in the rowdy protest. Several protesters were arrested and police said more arrests were pending.
One Nation spokesman David Ettridge said the protest was the worst he had ever seen at a Hanson rally, which traditionally attract noisy protesters who claim Hanson is fomenting racism.
Hanson's One Nation party, which has an anti-immigration platform, has attracted support away from Australia's main political parties to become the country's third political force.

An opinion poll published on Tuesday showed six-percent support for the independent politician and her party, which was only officially registered last week. Hanson is the only elected member of her party and it has yet to be tested at an election.
